findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent (fresh installs)
findings.body: The migration unconditionally does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. On any site that never set the `embed_category` site setting (including all fresh installs and test databases), the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and calling `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration entirely. The `embeddable_hosts` lookup below is guarded with `cmd_tuples > 0`, but the category lookup is not. The result string must be checked for emptiness before dereferencing.

findings.title: SQL injection / broken INSERT via unescaped host values in migration
findings.body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by string interpolation with no quoting. The host values come from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which was free-form text; a value containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) will either break the migration with a syntax error or inject arbitrary SQL. Use `sanitize_sql`/quote or ActiveRecord inserts instead.

findings.title: create_table uses force: true, silently dropping existing data
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists (e.g. if the migration is re-run in a weird state or the table was created by an earlier deploy), silently destroying all embeddable host rows. A fresh migration should not use `force: true`.

findings.title: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that pretends to save
findings.body: The `update` action is routed (PUT /admin/customize/embedding) and the frontend `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but the controller never reads params or persists anything — it just re-renders the current state. Any admin who hits save gets a success response while nothing is saved. Either persist the submitted attributes or remove the route/action until there is something to update.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when the id doesn't exist (e.g. the record was deleted in another tab). `save_host(nil)` then raises NoMethodError on `host.host =` and `destroy` raises on `host.destroy`, producing a 500 instead of a 404. Guard for a missing record and render not_found.

findings.title: Nil/blank host value causes NoMethodError before validation can report an error
findings.body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is assigned straight onto the record, and the model's `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)`. If `host` is nil (empty input or missing param), `sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request 500s instead of returning a validation error via `render_json_error`. Also note `sub!` on a frozen/nil value and the fact that `validates_format_of` would have handled a blank value if the callback didn't crash first.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host
findings.body: There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (and no unique index in the migration). An admin can save the same host twice; `record_for_host` then uses `.first`, so only one of the duplicate categories is ever used for embedding, and the second record silently shadows the first. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique index on lower(host).

findings.title: Host regex rejects valid hostnames and long TLDs
findings.body: The validation regex `\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` rejects hosts with TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. `.museum`, `.travel`, internationalized/punycode `xn--` labels), hosts with underscores, and `localhost`. Since before_validation strips schemes/paths anyway, the port/path portions of the regex are also dead weight. Valid-looking hosts will fail with a confusing format error.

findings.title: Fabricator contents are in swapped files
findings.body: The embeddable_host fabricator now lives in `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` while all the category fabricators were moved into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. It happens to work because Fabrication loads all files, but the file names no longer reflect their contents, which will confuse anyone looking for the category or embeddable_host fabricator definitions. The contents should be in the correctly named files.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no request specs
findings.body: Both new controller specs only assert the controller's superclass. There are no tests for create/update/destroy behavior: success serialization, validation error rendering (render_json_error), the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id, or authorization (only the route-level AdminConstraint is exercised). Given the nil-record and nil-host crash paths above, these endpoints are untested against real inputs.
